headline: Protein language and structure models are probed and used to expose evolutionary and structural signal
label: Protein Models And Evolutionary Structure
summary: Foundation models and AlphaFold are now being dissected and mined for evolutionary and physicochemical signal, with applications spanning design and phylogeny.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of learned protein representations as explicit carriers of evolutionary and structural information. The review of protein foundation models covers residue dependencies, pathogenicity and alignment-free evolutionary analysis. AlphaInterp examines AlphaFold 3 mechanistically, reporting that a few divergent MSA homologues suffice to recover structure, via pairformer latent geometry. The analysis of 373,779 AlphaFold structures finds organism-specific physicochemical signatures that recover tree-of-life features. Generative design of peptides with custom secondary structure motifs and reduced alphabets applies similar models prospectively, while MolEvolvR is a more conventional domain- and phylogeny-centric web tool and is less tied to learned representations. What is new is the shift from using these models as predictors to interrogating what latent evolutionary content they encode.
